title: Squad workload manifest (platform/v1)
description: What a squad asks the platform for. One file per squad at squads/<squad>/workload.yaml. The schema is the squad-facing API: anything not described here isn't something a squad can ask for through the manifest (they use their own infra/ folder for that, inside policy).

apiVersion.description: Versioned so the contract can change without breaking squads already on it. A v2 would sit beside v1 until every squad had moved.

squad.description: Becomes the resource group name (rg-squad-<squad>), the squad tag value, and the prefix on every shared resource (topics, API paths). Short and lowercase because several Azure names it feeds into are length-limited (Key Vault: 24 chars).

repository.description: The squad's code repo (owner/name). The squad deployer identity trusts OIDC tokens from this repo's 'production' GitHub environment and nothing else.

keyVault.description: One Key Vault, RBAC mode, private endpoint only. The function app gets Key Vault Secrets User.

appConfig.description: One Standard App Configuration store, private endpoint only. The function app gets App Configuration Data Reader. About $36/month each at list price, so off by default.

storage.description: Blob containers in one squad data storage account. The function app gets Storage Blob Data Contributor on each container, not the whole account.

topics.description: Topics this squad publishes, created in the shared namespace as <squad>.<topic>. The function app gets Data Sender on each topic only.

subscribe.description: Topics (any squad's, fully qualified as <squad>.<topic>) this squad consumes. Creates a subscription named after this squad. The function app gets Data Receiver on that subscription only.

expose.description: Publish the function's HTTP API through APIM and Front Door.

path.description: Single segment, e.g. /orders. Must be unique across all squads (checked by validate.mjs, which can see every manifest; the schema only sees one).
